images.caption: Figure 1:Learning and transferring spatial foresight.Demonstrations spanning 60 tasks and five spatial categories train an action-conditioned spatial world model to predict visual dynamics and 3D hand flow. The learned spatial foresight is transferred into a low-level policy, enabling action generation without world-model execution or future decoding at deployment. DexForesight outperforms prior world-action models in both simulation and real-robot evaluations.

Figure 2:DexForesight architecture and query alignment.The spatial world model learns action-conditioned hand motion and visual changes from RGB, offline scene depth, hand geometry, and language. Demonstrated controls condition the world queries through the query adapter and are also supplied to both prediction experts. Queries from the frozen world model supervise policy queries, which condition the action expert.
Figure 3:Real-robot data and training.Recording hours and example frames for the five task categories. The final stage uses 100 hours with depth estimated offline by StereoAnyVideo.

Figure 4:Experimental setup and tasks.Top: the Sharpa North robot with 22-DoF Sharpa Wave hands and the three real-robot tasks. Bottom: the Franka Panda with a 16-DoF Allegro hand and example simulation tasks.
